title: Kroger Co. beefs up bonuses for highest-paid bosses
summary: Kroger's top executives received significant compensation increases in 2018, primarily driven by larger cash bonuses tied to the company's "strong performance on adjusted earnings per share." CEO Rodney McMullen's total compensation rose 19 percent to $11.7 million, including a $2.7 million bonus. This occurred as Kroger adapted to increased competition and invested heavily in technology and store remodeling under its Restock Kroger initiative.

title: Cereal Killer: Kellogg’s Must Transform Its Company to Survive—Will It Succeed?
summary: This article analyzes Kellogg's need for significant transformation to survive and thrive amidst changing consumer preferences and declining U.S. cereal demand. It discusses CEO Steve Cahillane's "Deploy for Growth" strategy, recent divestitures and acquisitions, and proposes bold recommendations including divestment of most U.S. cereal brands, capabilities-driven M&A, and radical innovation in food production and delivery, emphasizing a shift from a "Day Two" to a "Day One" company culture.

title: Amazon Can't Duck Williams-Sonoma Suit Over Furniture Sales
summary: Amazon.com Inc. failed to dismiss a trademark infringement lawsuit filed by Williams-Sonoma. Williams-Sonoma alleges that Amazon's "Rivet" line includes products "strikingly similar" to its West Elm brand and that Amazon's website misleads customers into thinking it's an authorized reseller. A judge ruled that the trademark-infringement claims are a "close call," allowing the suit to proceed to determine if consumers are confused by Amazon's listings.

title: Target rebrands digital-advertising business as Roundel
summary: Target has rebranded its digital advertising business from Target Media Network to Roundel, signaling an aggressive push into the digital advertising sector. The company aims to leverage its customer data and "exceptional branding" to offer personalized ad campaigns for its 1,000 clients, including major brands like Disney and Coca-Cola. This move positions Target to compete more directly with other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which have also seen success in their advertising businesses.

title: Major Carriers Strive to Automate Loading and Unloading Trucks
summary: Major carriers like FedEx and UPS are investing in automation to streamline the crucial but challenging process of loading and unloading trucks, particularly due to the varied nature of packages. Honeywell and Siemens AG have developed distinct solutions: Honeywell's mobile unit uses suction cups, while Siemens' system requires a permanent rolling belt in the trailer. These innovations aim to improve efficiency and employee satisfaction, though market availability dates are yet to be announced.

title: Robots edging closer to the key task of unloading trucks
summary: FedEx and UPS are investing in robots to automate truck unloading as e-commerce surges and Amazon expands its logistics. Companies like Honeywell and Siemens have developed machines that can unload trucks as fast as humans, mitigating the strenuous nature of the job. While unloading is closer to being solved, companies like Dorabot are also making progress on the more complex task of automating truck loading.

title: QEDIT Partners With Ant Financial, VMware, RGAX, Raises $10 Million
summary: QEDIT, a company specializing in privacy layers for enterprise blockchain networks, has announced partnerships with Ant Financial, VMware Inc., and RGAX. Simultaneously, QEDIT closed a $10 million Series A funding round led by MizMaa Ventures, with participation from its new partners and other investors. This funding will support the development of its privacy protocol and expand sales and partnerships, aiming to enhance data protection and efficiency in the finance and insurance industries.

title: Teamsters Call for XPO Logistics to Separate Board Chairman, CEO Roles
summary: The International Brotherhood of Teamsters is urging XPO Logistics to separate the roles of board chairman and CEO, advocating for an independent director to chair the board. This comes after XPO's stock plunged and the company lost significant business, leading the Teamsters to express concerns about concentrated power in one individual, current Chairman and CEO Bradley Jacobs. Two shareholder advisory firms, Glass Lewis & Co. and Institutional Shareholder Services, are supporting the Teamsters' resolution.

title: Synchronoss teams with Amazon to provide integration service to operators
summary: Synchronoss Technologies has partnered with Amazon to streamline the way mobile operators offer Amazon's services to their customers, integrated directly into carrier billing systems. Utilizing its Digital Experience Platform (DXP), Synchronoss will act as an integrator to make the process more efficient for both Amazon and global carriers. This collaboration aims to simplify customer journeys and accelerate the time to market for Amazon services through a carrier's existing infrastructure.

title: Former Humana employee pleads guilty to federal fraud charges
summary: A former Humana employee, Nitin More, pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges. The charges relate to More copying thousands of Amazon access codes that were intended for use as rewards in Humana's Go365 fitness program.

title: 20s Jonathan Morley
authors: ['John R. Boehm and Stephen J. Serio', 'Lynne Marek']
summary: Jonathan Morley, a lead software engineer at CME Group, is recognized for his contributions to emerging technologies including supporting the rollout of bitcoin futures. He is also noted for his passion for learning and teaching, having authored books on blockchain and Big Data, and for his leadership in establishing CME's employee networking group PRIDE. His ability to bridge technology and business perspectives, along with his community involvement, distinguishes him in his field.

title: Supermicro moves production from China
summary: Supermicro is reportedly moving its production facilities out of China due to lingering customer concerns about embedded spy chips in its motherboards, despite being cleared by investigations. This decision also serves to mitigate the impact of the U.S.-China trade war. The company is expanding manufacturing in Taiwan and California to increase self-reliance and meet customer demand.

title: QVC chief says ‘we’re living in a changing world’ as shares plunge on disappointing results
summary: Qurate Retail, Inc. (QRTEA) shares plunged nearly 27 percent after the company reported a disappointing 4 percent decrease in overall revenue for the first quarter, totaling about $3.1 billion. CEO Mike George attributed the decline to a changing retail and media landscape, including shifts in consumer shopping habits and the integration challenges of the HSN acquisition. An analyst noted that these market trends have been ongoing for years, questioning why their impact was more pronounced in the first quarter for Qurate's brands like QVC, HSN, Zulily, and Cornerstone Brands.

title: Supreme Court Deals Blow to Apple in Antitrust Case
summary: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that App Store customers have the standing to sue Apple for antitrust violations, rejecting Apple's argument that customers purchase apps from third-party developers directly. The decision allows a 2011 lawsuit alleging Apple drives up app prices through a 30 percent commission to proceed, potentially impacting other companies that operate as marketplaces. The ruling clarifies the "direct purchaser" principle under antitrust law but does not overturn the Illinois Brick doctrine.

title: Exploring the Republic Services of Southern Nevada Recycling Facility
summary: This article details a tour of the Republic Services of Southern Nevada recycling facility and learning center. It highlights the facility's operations, advanced technologies for sorting materials, educational challenges in an "immature recycling market," and its commitment to sustainability. The facility processes 2 million pounds of materials daily, separating commercial and residential streams and employing optical sorters and quality control measures.

title: Enabling digital success with APIs and Microservices
summary: This article discusses how APIs and microservices are crucial for digital success in modern organizations by enabling collaboration, innovation, and scalable, resilient systems. It highlights the challenges of legacy IT assets and provides an approach for successful API and microservices implementation based on five key pillars. The piece also explains the roles of APIs and microservices in driving better customer experiences and achieving zero-downtime service availability.

title: Disney to buy full control of Hulu from NBC owner Comcast
summary: Disney is taking full operational control of the streaming service Hulu from Comcast in a deal that values Hulu at $27.5 billion U.S. This move positions Disney to better compete with Netflix, especially as Disney prepares to launch its own streaming service, Disney+. The agreement allows Disney to acquire Comcast's remaining 33 percent stake after January 2024.

title: Dolby Appoints Anjali Sud to its Board of Directors
summary: Dolby Laboratories, Inc. announced the appointment of Anjali Sud, CEO of Vimeo, to its Board of Directors as a new independent director, effective May 13, 2019. Sud brings extensive knowledge of the technology industry and operational experience, filling a vacancy left by the passing of former director Nicholas Donatiello, Jr. Her background at Vimeo and Amazon.com is expected to greatly strengthen the Board.

title: Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:ESGV)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF (ESGV), including its current price, key statistics, fund overview, expenses, and recent news headlines. It highlights ESGV's investment strategy, which focuses on U.S. all-cap companies screened for environmental, social, and corporate governance criteria, and lists its top holdings and sector exposure. The fund, managed by Vanguard, has assets under management of $11.58 billion and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: NICE Acquires Brand Embassy
summary: NICE has acquired Brand Embassy, a Prague-based company specializing in omnichannel cloud-based customer service platforms. Brand Embassy's technology integrates social media, messaging, live chat, and AI-powered chatbots, serving approximately 80 customers including Telefonica O2 and Vodafone. This acquisition will enable NICE inContact to adopt a digital-first approach within its CXone platform, de-coupling voice from digital channels and creating new sales opportunities for enterprises looking to unify digital engagement solutions.

title: Stanley Black & Decker investing $90M to shift more Craftsman production back to US
summary: Stanley Black & Decker is investing $90 million to open a new 425,000-square-foot facility in Fort Worth, Texas, to bring more Craftsman production back to the U.S. This initiative aims to revitalize the iconic American brand and expand its manufacturing heritage, with the goal of reaching $1 billion in incremental revenues by 2021. The plant will employ about 500 full-time workers and incorporate advanced manufacturing technologies.

title: Microsoft, Sony partner on streaming games, chips and AI
summary: Microsoft and Sony have announced a strategic partnership where Sony will leverage Microsoft's cloud services, specifically Azure, for game and media streaming. The collaboration also extends to co-developing image sensors and integrating Microsoft's AI technology into Sony's consumer products. This deal aims to bolster Microsoft's cloud business and provide Sony's gaming platform with enhanced streaming capabilities, especially as its PlayStation 4 nears the end of its lifecycle.

title: JP Morgan buys health-care payments firm InstaMed in the bank's biggest acquisition since the financial crisis
summary: J.P. Morgan Chase is acquiring InstaMed, a healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million, making it the bank's largest acquisition since the financial crisis. This move aims to deepen J.P. Morgan's presence in the $3.5 trillion U.S. health-care spending market and underscores the bank's aggressive strategy in the evolving world of payments. InstaMed, founded in 2004, automates medical billing and processed $94 billion in transactions last year.

title: JPMorgan to buy healthcare payments technology firm InstaMed
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced its plan to acquire InstaMed, a U.S. healthcare payments technology firm, for over $500 million. This acquisition is part of JPMorgan's deeper dive into the $3.5 trillion healthcare market, aiming to expand its payment services for healthcare consumers, providers, and payers, and to leverage InstaMed's established network and platform to address inefficiencies in healthcare payments. The deal is expected to integrate JPMorgan’s payment infrastructure into InstaMed, potentially also leveraging the bank's healthcare venture, Haven, with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway.

title: Cray, the Seattle-based supercomputer pioneer, sold to HPE for $1.3 billion
summary: Seattle-based supercomputer maker Cray has agreed to be acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) for $1.3 billion, or $35 per share, representing a 17.4% premium. This acquisition aims to combine Cray's supercomputing expertise and market position in academia and government with HPE's broader portfolio, bolstering HPE's capabilities in high-end computing and next-generation technology development, especially in the context of cloud computing and AI. The deal, which is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, is intended to help Cray address challenges of scale and investment in its "exascale" systems roadmap, despite recent contract wins.

title: Walmart’s digital efforts paying off in battle with Amazon
summary: Walmart's first-quarter results indicate its digital efforts are successfully gaining e-commerce market share against competitor Amazon.com Inc. The company reported a 37% growth in e-commerce sales and an increased inventory to support fulfillment centers, as CEO Doug McMillon emphasized Walmart's evolution into "more of a digital enterprise." These strategic moves, including new online brands and improved customer interfaces, highlight Walmart's commitment to strengthening its online presence.

title: Colgate-Palmolive tops Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain rankings
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has secured the top position in Gartner’s 2019 Supply Chain Top 25 rankings, moving up from fourth place in 2018 due to strong financial performance and focus on corporate social responsibility. Alibaba and Akzo Nobel also made their debut on the shortlist. Unilever joined the "Masters" category after consistently ranking in the top five for seven consecutive years, recognized for its advanced digital supply chain processes and use of emerging technologies.

title: Coca-Cola Will Revive New Coke in Alliance With Netflix, ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Coca-Cola is reviving New Coke for a limited time as part of a partnership with Netflix, integrating the infamous beverage into the third season of "Stranger Things," which is set in 1985. This marketing initiative aims to promote both the return of the series and gives Coca-Cola a unique way to connect with streaming audiences, despite New Coke's historical marketing failure. Coca-Cola will make 500,000 cans available online and in select locations, also releasing limited-edition original Coke with "Stranger Things" designs.

title: Lions Gate is still interested in selling Starz to CBS — then might have to merge with MGM to stay relevant
summary: Lions Gate is still interested in selling its premium entertainment network Starz to CBS, with talks expected to continue. If the Starz sale goes through, Lions Gate may consider a merger with MGM to gain scale and remain relevant as a standalone public company. The consolidation trend among smaller media companies is driven by competition from tech giants like Netflix and Amazon.

title: Baidu Tops China’s Smart Speaker Market and Enters Top 3 Globally in First Quarter
summary: Baidu, Inc. emerged as the top smart speaker vendor in China and a global top-three player in Q1 2019, according to Canalys and Strategy Analytics, driven by the strong performance of its DuerOS conversational AI system. China has surpassed the U.S. as the largest smart speaker market with 500% year-on-year growth. Baidu's DuerOS voice assistant base reached 275 million users, with monthly voice queries increasing significantly, indicating strong user engagement and product innovation.

title: This millennial used scholarship money to buy property in college—now his real estate company is worth $3.8 billion
summary: Eric Wu, co-founder and CEO of Opendoor, used his college scholarship money to buy his first property at age 19. He expanded his real estate portfolio to about 25 properties by the time he graduated, leveraging equity and rental income. This early venture into real estate and tech led him to co-found Opendoor, a real estate startup now valued at $3.8 billion.

title: How Costco uses $5 rotisserie chickens and free samples to turn customers into fanatics
summary: Costco cultivates immense customer loyalty through strategic design elements including exclusive memberships, extreme value (like $5 rotisserie chickens), and an engaging "treasure hunt" shopping experience. The company's low prices, unique store layout, free samples, and popular Kirkland Signature brand contribute to high customer retention and strong financial performance. Ultimately, Costco's business model focuses on providing high-quality products at low prices while making a fair return, leading to billions in revenue.

title: Monro expands partnership with Amazon with 800 Monro centers
summary: Monro Auto Service and Tire Centers announced the expansion of its partnership with Amazon.com, allowing tire installation services at over 400 additional retail locations. This expansion more than doubles the number of service locations to over 800 stores across 21 states, representing approximately two-thirds of Monro's store base. The collaboration has received an average 4.6-star rating and is a key initiative in Monro's omni-channel strategy.

title: Lands’ End to take final steps away from Sears
summary: Lands' End is nearing its complete separation from Sears by exiting its remaining store-within-a-store locations. The apparel retailer plans to open 40 to 60 owned stores in the coming years and has expanded its online presence, including selling on Amazon and Walmart.com. Analysts widely support this move, citing Sears' declining relevance and the benefits of Lands' End strengthening its own brand and direct-to-consumer channels.

title: Palo Alto Networks Introduces Prisma: The Secure Way to Cloud
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Prisma, a new cloud security suite designed to provide simpler, more secure, and comprehensive cloud security. Prisma consolidates and expands on existing cloud security products, offering solutions for secure access, data protection, and application security across various cloud environments. With approximately 9,000 enterprise customers, Prisma aims to be the largest cloud security business globally.

title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Cloud Container Security Provider Twistlock: Report -
summary: Palo Alto Networks has reportedly acquired Twistlock, an Israel-based cybersecurity startup specializing in container, serverless, and public cloud system protection, for an estimated $450 million to $500 million. This acquisition comes just before Palo Alto Networks' Ignite19 conference and follows other strategic moves to expand its MSSP-centric partner program. Twistlock's technology protects major cloud systems like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, and Pivotal.

title: SETTING THE STAGE
summary: The article discusses the resurgence of film and television production in Los Angeles, driven by streaming services and tax incentives, which has led to a boom for soundstage owners. It highlights that studio spaces are near 100% occupancy, making it a lucrative but operationally intensive business for property owners. Key players like Hudson Pacific Properties, Occidental Entertainment Group, and Hackman Capital are expanding their soundstage portfolios, with long-term leases becoming more common due to high demand.

title: 'Merch by Amazon' t-shirt business increasing orders from Disney to Dr. Seuss
summary: Amazon's 'Merch by Amazon' on-demand t-shirt printing service is increasingly being used by major entertainment companies like Walt Disney Co and Dr. Seuss. This service allows brands to produce merchandise closer to the point of sale, eliminating the need for large upfront inventory commitments and traditional supply chains. The trend is contributing to Amazon's growing influence in the clothing industry and allows for more niche and timely product offerings.

title: Exclusive: Amazon interested in buying Boost from T-Mobile, Sprint - sources
summary: Amazon.com Inc is reportedly interested in acquiring Boost Mobile from T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp, according to sources familiar with the matter. The potential deal would allow Amazon to utilize the new T-Mobile's wireless network for at least six years and could also include the divestment of wireless spectrum. This move comes as T-Mobile and Sprint look to sell assets like Boost to gain regulatory approval for their planned $26 billion merger.
